note: One kind of scene, several arcs (owner, Nov 8, 9:50 voice note: 'they've gotta have like a variance. So even though there's only 5 in corruption scenes right now, you could get, I'm just making a number up, 30 different scenes within there'). A family is a purpose in purpose-arcs.json; its variants are the arcs it can play. src/director/arc-variant.ts scores each variant from the records, as an address's kind is scored (address-kinds.json): a variant's score is its base plus each term's weight times a read between 0 and 1 (`low` reads one minus the read), never below nothing, times one plus the asker's pull toward it (the mean of the personality facets listed). The highest score plays and a tie goes to the name first in the alphabet; no roll, no threshold. A read looks at the records in one of six ways: a number kept on a module's row that the cause record names (`record`), a number the cause record itself carries (`fact`), how close the two people are (`closeness`), how many earlier records of some kinds name both people, optionally only those whose facts match (`history`), the asker's money pressure (`strain`), or where the scene is set (`setting`). A variant holds the arc (state, replies, follow, again, endings: moves only, no sentence) and the purpose id its bank pieces are written under; the family's own pieces serve where it has none of its own. Ending ids the engines read downstream (took-it, put-off, left-there, said-you-would-report) keep their meaning in every variant; a variant's other endings are refusals to the engine. Every weight is TUNABLE and registered as SG-STORY-arc-variant-weights.

scale.checkedAgainst: The offerer's own weighing of the favor, its worth against a year of their living costs on a log scale (corruption.ts offerValues.stake): at 1 the favor is worth about one and three quarters of their year, and the read is one half.
One earlier refusal reads one half, two read two thirds: the second ask is already a different scene, the fifth only a little more.
As refused-before, for offers to the same seat from the same person.
As refused-before, for earlier pressure from the same person on the same seat.

of.checkedAgainst: The gift against the donor's own year of living costs: at one twentieth of a year the read is one half, so a gift of a few hundred dollars reads small and one of several thousand reads large for most households.

scale.checkedAgainst: As refused-before, for earlier gifts from the same donor to the same candidate.
As refused-before, for an earlier donor-ask between the same two people that the candidate put off.
One earlier answer on the record to the same reporter reads one half, two read two thirds: a reporter who has taken the player's words twice already covers them.
As answered-before, for earlier talks between the same two that ended in a quarrel.
As answered-before, for earlier talks between the same two where the player would not comment.

within.checkedAgainst: A story the press printed about the player in the last half year is still open; one from years ago is a closed matter.

scale.checkedAgainst: As answered-before, for stories the press printed about the player's own conduct.
One reported bribe or conviction reads one half: a single story is already a different interview.

One earlier bill of the player's own that the asker voted for reads one half, two read two thirds: a colleague who has voted with the player once already has a favor to call in, and the second adds less than the first.
As refused-before, for earlier quarrels between the same two people that the records name: one earlier quarrel reads one half, so the second is already a different scene.

within.checkedAgainst: A layoff in the last half year is still the reason they are at the table; one from years ago is only part of their history.

scale.checkedAgainst: One layoff in the window reads two thirds, a second reads four fifths: the person who lost a job this spring is already the person who lost a job.
